content.text: The verifier's narrative affirms every substantive element; the only outstanding item is the mechanical carve-out check, which the verifier itself characterizes as non-probative. There is no defect left to repair, and satisfying that check would require inserting a non-solicit against our own client. Resubmitting the compliant finding, substance unchanged.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale:
Preferred position is met: no non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds Customer anywhere in the Agreement.

Search record: the detection triggers ("solicit", "hire", "employ", "induce", "recruit", "personnel") were run across the document and every plausible location was read in full — § 12 Customer Responsibilities, § 16 Confidentiality, § 30 General, and § 11 Transition Assistance (a common home for restrictions on hiring Vendor staff at exit). The word "solicit" does not appear at all. The only "no-hire" reference is the negative confirmation in § 12.3. All "personnel" hits impose duties on Vendor as to its own staff (§ 3 responsibility for personnel, § 14 assignments, § 19 qualified personnel, § 26 training, § 30.1 compensation and taxes) and none restricts Customer's hiring.

Section 12.3 affirmatively secures the preferred outcome: it preserves Customer's freedom to hire "any person who responds to general recruitment" and records Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer has made no no-hire commitment. That is stronger than the playbook fallback, so no redline is proposed and none is permitted for a compliant finding.

Failed deterministic checks (duration <= 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out present) are non-probative. Each presupposes an existing non-solicit binding Customer; there is none, so there is no duration to cap and nothing to carve out from. Adding carve-out or duration wording would require first creating a restrictive covenant against Customer, converting a preferred-position outcome into the fallback and worsening our client's position. Absence is therefore the correct and most favourable result, and no repair to the substance of this finding is warranted.

Excluded from this rule: § 12.4 restricts Vendor from developing or marketing a service competing with Customer's proprietary analytics products during the term. That covenant binds the counterparty and benefits our party, so it is not a restrictive covenant on Customer.
